title: Protein Interactome Analysis of Small Non-Coding Vault RNAs via Mass Spectrometry
author: van der Kooij, Stok, et al.
materials: Follow-up analysis regarding the quantification and visualization of the individual protein hits is performed with Perseus software. Stratify the data per individual vtRNA and based on experimental conditions (i.e., mock versus infected cells). We recommend to perform RAP-MS in duplicate, and preferably triplicate, experiments. Only proteins that are identified in all replicate experiments should be included in downstream analysis. As a quality control of the reproducibility of the data a Pearson correlation coefficient can be calculated (Figure 1). Ideally, a strong correlation for the “hits” should be observed between two replicate experiments. The approximate enrichment of vtRNA-specific interactors is measured by calculating the fold change between the antisense pulldown (vtRNA1-1, vtRNA1-2 or vtRNA1-3) and the respective sense pulldown (negative control), by comparing the log-corrected and normalized intensities from the antisense pulldown to the log-corrected normalized proteins in the sense pulldown. It is not uncommon that the obtained vtRNA interactomes share a high degree of similarity across the different vtRNAs. Furthermore, the proteins retrieved with the sense probe may have a certain degree of overlap with the proteins isolated with the anti-sense probe. Solutions to these two issues are discussed in “Problem 4” and “Problem 5”, respectively. The analyzed dataset is attached in the supplementary data, while the raw dataset containing the peptide counts and coverage can be found in Stok et al., 2025.1Figure 1Reproducibility between RAP-MS replicatesProteins identified in the antisense pulldown of vtRNA1-1 are plotted for each replicate experiment on different axes with a log-transformed relative abundance. The Pearson correlation coefficient between the replicate experiments was calculated and displayed as r value.

steps.title: UV crosslink and freeze cell pellets
steps.instruction: After 24 h infection, aspirate medium, wash cells with 10 mL ice‑cold PBS, add another 10 mL ice‑cold PBS, irradiate in a UVP crosslinker at 254 nm with 0.8 J/cm² (pre‑warm bulb with an empty run at 0.3 J/cm²), keep plates on ice, scrape cells with a cell lifter, collect in a DNA LoBind 50 mL tube, centrifuge 5 min at 1000 g at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant, snap‑freeze the pellet on dry‑ice and store at –80 °C (max 1 month). Perform all subsequent steps on ice, using RNase‑free reagents, DNA LoBind tips/tubes, freshly opened buffers, and a clean bench to avoid protein contamination.

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin beads for capture
steps.instruction: For each pulldown, aliquot 300 µL streptavidin‑coated magnetic beads (100 µL for pre‑clearing, 200 µL for probe capture). Wash beads four times with 900 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, then twice with 900 µL 1× Hybridization buffer using a DynaMag‑2 magnet. Resuspend beads in 300 µL 1× Hybridization buffer and add BSA to a final concentration of 0.01 mg/mL (1 % w/v stock). Block beads by end‑over‑end rotation for 16 h at 4 °C. (Total bead volume required for two conditions with six pulldowns each is 3.6 mL.)

steps.title: Process protein samples for mass spectrometry
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry each eluate for 1–2 h (optionally freeze in liquid N₂ first). Resuspend the dried pellet in 16 µL UltraPure water (pellet ≈2 µL). Add 6 µL 4× protein sample buffer, boil 95 °C for 5 min. Load samples onto a 4–15 % Mini‑PROTEAN™ TGX™ Precast gel and run at 80 V until the front migrates ~1 cm. Use pre‑cast gels, leave an empty lane between samples, and load only sense and antisense pulldown lanes (inputs/unbound are saved for QC). Fix the gel with the SilverQuest silver‑staining kit per manufacturer. Slice each lane into 5 equal sections, cut sections into small blocks, wash blocks with PBS, reduce with 10 mM dithiothreitol, alkylate with 50 mM iodoacetamide. Digest in‑gel with trypsin (12.5 ng/µL) for 16 h at 37 °C using a Proteineer DP robot. Extract peptides, lyophilize, and store at –80 °C (max 1 month). Resuspend peptides in water/0.1 % formic acid (100/0.1 % v/v) and analyse by LC‑MS/MS on an Ultimate 3000 nano‑gradient system coupled to an Exploris 480 mass spectrometer. Use a 300 µm × 5 mm C18 PepMap (5 µm, 100 Å) pre‑column and a 50 cm × 75 µm Reprosil‑Pur C18‑AQ (1.9 µm, 120 Å) analytical column.

steps.title: Prepare RNA for pull‑down efficiency assay
steps.instruction: Separate the supernatant of the RNA elution with a DynaMag‑2 magnet, resuspend the beads in 20 µL NLS Elution buffer, heat 2 min at 95 °C, re‑separate beads, and transfer the supernatant (RNA) to a new PCR tube. Equalise all RNA sample volumes with NLS Elution buffer. Thaw input and unbound samples, add proteinase K to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL and incubate 1 h at 55 °C. Samples may be stored at –80 °C for up to 1 month before SILANE clean‑up. Proceed to qPCR or Northern blot as desired.

steps.title: Extract RNA, synthesize cDNA, and qPCR
steps.instruction: Thaw proteinase K‑treated RNA on ice. For each isolation, aliquot 20 µL Dynabeads™ MyOne™ Silane beads, discard the storage buffer with a DynaMag‑PCR magnet and resuspend beads in 60 µL RLT buffer. Add the bead suspension to the 20 µL RNA sample and mix. Add 120 µL 100 % ethanol, incubate 2 min at 22 °C to bind RNA, then magnetically separate and wash beads twice with 200 µL 100 % ethanol. Air‑dry beads ~5 min, elute RNA in 20 µL TURBO DNase elution buffer (20 min at 37 °C), then perform a second Silane extraction as above but elute in 10 µL UltraPure water. Store RNA at –80 °C. Synthesize cDNA using 5 µL RNA with SuperScript IV VILO Master Mix (any equivalent kit is acceptable; DNase step not required). Perform qPCR with vtRNA‑specific primers, PowerUp™ SYBR™ Green Master Mix, and a QuantStudio 3 (or equivalent) following the manufacturer’s protocol to assess viral infection, vtRNA up‑regulation, and pull‑down efficiency.

steps.title: Identify proteins using Mascot
steps.instruction: Convert raw MS data to a peak list (mass, charge, intensity) with Proteome Discoverer. Search the list against a minimal UniProt database supplemented with EMCV polyprotein (or other viral) sequences using Mascot with the following settings: precursor mass tolerance 10 ppm, fragment mass tolerance 0.02 Da, enzyme trypsin, variable modifications methionine oxidation and N‑terminal acetylation, fixed modification carbamidomethyl on cysteines, false‑discovery rate < 1 %.

steps.title: Filter contaminants and low‑peptide proteins
steps.instruction: From the Mascot results, remove common contaminants such as benzonase, BSA, and keratin. Exclude any protein identified with fewer than two unique peptides.

steps.title: Quantify and statistically analyze interactome data
steps.instruction: Import the filtered protein list into Perseus. Stratify data by vtRNA (vtRNA1‑1, vtRNA1‑2, vtRNA1‑3) and condition (mock vs infected). Perform RAP‑MS in duplicate or triplicate and retain only proteins present in all replicates. Calculate Pearson correlation coefficients between replicates as a quality control. Compute fold‑change enrichment of antisense versus sense pulldowns by comparing log‑corrected, normalized intensities; report only proteins meeting the reproducibility criteria. Visualise results as needed.
